rule_results.rationale: Applicable: Petclinic runs in an application pod. The pinned workload has no required security settings and the source has no container build establishing a non-root user. The later platform Deployment is a reference, not proof for this commit.
Applicable: the application serves HTTP. Its pinned manifest uses NodePort, an explicit assessment failure, although the later platform reference supplies a Traefik route.

Applicable: the application depends on PostgreSQL. The legacy manifest has distinct paths but does not include db in readiness; official Spring Boot 4.1 documentation confirms it is not included by default. The selected platform reference does include it.

Applicable: Petclinic has a PostgreSQL driver and relational data. Its pinned source supplies an app-owned database, a legacy binding to that database, and a localhost profile fallback; these meet DP-05 assessment fail conditions despite the later CloudNativePG reference.

Applicable: the application has PostgreSQL schema and seed SQL. The pinned PostgreSQL profile performs startup SQL, an assessment failure. The existing platform PreSync Job and deployment override do not erase this independent source setting.

Applicable: the application needs database credentials. The pinned legacy Kubernetes Secret and active legacy PostgreSQL profile include literal credentials. The later GitOps reference correctly uses an operator-generated Secret but does not make the pinned source pass.

Applicable: this application is delivered through GitOps on the selected platform. The pinned application retains direct Kind deployment of incompatible manifests, while the later platform pipeline supplies the intended digest promotion.

Applicable: the pinned source defines an application container. Its legacy container specification has no resources.requests; the later platform reference declares both requests but does not make the earlier manifest compliant.
